movements.name: ASCENSION
movements.what: How the site learned to think, and then to speak.
movements.note: Sixteen chapters in four acts, prologue included. Opens in medias res on failure and ends at a threshold deliberately uncrossed.

movements.name: THE LONG CLIMB
movements.what: The threshold crossed. The helix, and the black heart of Page 2.
movements.note: The one movement that is finished — typeset and illustrated. It also spans the UNDOCUMENTED PERIOD: no briefs before 29 June.

movements.name: THE SIEGE
movements.what: Three days. The gates were not breached — they were read.
movements.source: The Siege.html — 6,651 words, nine books plus a field journal
movements.note: The gates were closed by TIME, not an enemy. You cannot out-fight time, only outwork it — which is why the fleet is instruments rather than warships.

movements.name: THE SHIP
movements.what: Registers, probes, watches, the ark. The system becomes readable.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.blurb: Fifty miles above the Catskills, a man fires himself into the Hudson to find a door — and the door takes him.
chapters.why: RECONNAISSANCE, before the Siege. One man, one craft, no fleet. It ends with two years of lost probes returning out of the dark — they had not failed, they had gone on working with nobody to report to — and with the realisation that the doorway was an ACCESS POINT on a network running inside the rock. That is what makes the assault necessary. The tone-setter: exact machinery, real geography, and the ancient thing arriving as a finding rather than a flourish.

chapters.title: The Beach
chapters.blurb: A man comes out of the sea holding the only object that can release a thousand souls, and what he wants is a cheeseburger.
chapters.why: THE FRAME, and it belongs to no movement — what he reads is all four. It comes SECOND, after the Descent, so the reader has already been handed a piece of the record before learning it was commissioned. Opened once and never closed. The last human scene in the work, and the one chapter with no apparatus because it makes no claim a probe could check.

chapters.title: The Sound of a Sawmill
chapters.blurb: Parler-TTS in a Colab notebook producing a grinding mechanical roar instead of a voice. The dream of a speaking library, and the wall.
chapters.why: WRITE THIS FIRST — the author's own build order: lock the tone before proceeding. Ends on the question that reframes everything: what if one machine was never meant to both think and speak? Needs the 19 June transcript.
